transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

It is actually quite normal for plastics to remain damp in many dishwashers, including Bosch models. Plastic holds very little heat compared to ceramic or glass, so it doesn't get hot enough during the cycle to evaporate water droplets effectively; this is a physical property of the material, not necessarily a fault. However, if your glasses and china are also wet, or if you want better drying results, there are two quick checks we can do. First, rinse aid is essential for drying as it helps water sheet off dishes rather than sit in droplets—has yours run low recently? Second, programmes like 'Eco' or 'Quick' often skip the high-heat final dry phase to save energy. If you are using one of these, trying a standard cycle with hot wash and hot rinse usually improves drying significantly. Are your glasses also wet, or just the plastic tubs?
Some droplets on the glasses and cups too, not just the plastics. I use Eco 50 every time, and the rinse aid symbol is lit on the display. I use all-in-one tablets though.

[Heading: Rinse aid issue or programme setting]
The rinse aid symbol being lit on your display means the tank is actually empty. Even though you are using all-in-one tablets (which contain some rinse aid), that amount is often not enough for Bosch dishwashers to achieve good drying results, especially on Eco programmes which don't use a heated dry phase. If it's empty, top it up with liquid rinse aid. Also, if there is a dial inside that compartment, turn it to at least setting 3 or 4. This will help water sheet off your glasses and plastic tubs so they dry much faster.
Ok, I'll get some liquid rinse aid and fill it up. Is there anything else I should change, like settings on the machine?

[Heading: Insufficient rinse aid and Eco programme drying profile]
Yes, there are two key settings to adjust. First, ensure the rinse aid dial inside the dispenser is set to at least 3 or 4; this helps water sheet off your glasses so they dry properly. Second, try using a standard programme with 'Hot Wash' and 'Hot Rinse' options enabled instead of Eco 50. Eco cycles skip the heated drying phase to save energy, which is why you are seeing wetness on both glass and plastic. Once you have topped up the rinse aid and switched to a hotter cycle for a load, your results should improve significantly.
